newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada finance official puzzled by Martin rumors.
newsitem.headline: Canada finance official puzzled by Martin rumors.

text.p: Rumors in Canadian financial markets that Finance Minister Paul Martin might step down are puzzling, a senior Finance official said on Wednesday.

"I can't confirm that he'll be reappointed minister of finance. Only the prime minister can do that," assistant deputy minister Peter Daniel said in a telephone interview. "I don't know where all this comes from. We're quite surprised to hear all this."
He said he had spoken with other senior officials in the department and no one knew where the rumors came from.
Canadian bonds opened softer on Wednesday, partly on worries that Martin would not be reappointed finance minister when newly re-elected Prime Minister Jean Chretien named his cabinet next week.
Martin has won international praise for cutting Canada's deficit and helping boost Canada's economy.
The Liberal government was re-elected with a slim majority on Monday.
Chretien was evasive on Wednesday about whether Martin would retain his post.
Asked to reassure the markets that Martin would say on, Chretien told Reuters: "You know, he is the minister of finance. So if I make any change it will be known next week."
